idiom_name: tagged object ({ ok: true, value } / { ok: false, reason }) plus a match helper
implementation_notes: JavaScript has no sum types, so the pattern is a small module with two constructors that return tagged objects and one match/fold helper taking a handler per branch, so exactly one code path runs; JSDoc typedefs can document the tag, but nothing enforces it at runtime. The language's own error mechanism is throw/try/catch with Error objects (now carrying a cause), and FP-oriented teams use fp-ts's Either, which supplies map/flatMap/alt and the same Left/Right convention. Keep the hand-rolled form where failure is an expected branch that callers must render or branch on, and throw everywhere else.
pitfalls: Nothing stops a caller from reading .value on an error branch and letting undefined flow on: keep the constructors in one module, freeze the objects and never assemble them inline in feature code.

A thrown Error is not a value - it unwinds - so mixing throw in the same API forces callers to handle both channels; when converting, keep the Error itself as the reason instead of a formatted string.
Async code needs an explicit conversion step: an awaited rejection must be caught and turned into an err(...) value, otherwise the failure escapes the caller's branch handling entirely.
The tag is erased by a JSON round-trip, so anything arriving over the wire has to be validated (zod/ajv) before it is treated as an Either - a type annotation buys nothing at runtime.
